title: review: Skip the merge re-gate when the target has not moved since the daemon gate: gate() records the target and head it gated, merge() reuses that green result when the rebase was a no-op
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B9. Every merge runs the full gate again (merge.py gate.run_gate after the rebase) even when the daemon gated the identical tree minutes earlier against the same target head; on luna-inbox the Apple gate takes 9-11 min, so each task costs two gate runs.

Facts (goal/T-1403 at 92c1a98 plus B6 T-1551 merged before this task; re-check line numbers by symbol):
- daemon.py:1396 gate(pool): runs gate.run_gate(worktree, script=merge.TESTS_GREEN, task_id, cfg) and on green stamps 'gated_at' (grep "stamp(t[\"id\"], \"gated_at\"" in gate()); it does not record which target sha or worktree head it gated.
- merge.py:28-122 merge(): rebase onto target (46), then gate.run_gate (62) unconditionally, then fast-forward. _diff_hash (11-21) and the reviewed_sha check already compare before/after rebase.
- gate.run_gate returns {'returncode', 'timed_out', 'stdout', 'stderr', ...} (gate.py).

Change:
1. daemon.gate(): on a green run, the gated_at stamp also writes pipeline.gated_target_sha = rev-parse of the merge target (goal/<parent>, or 'integration' without a parent, same rule as merge.py:30) and pipeline.gated_head = rev-parse HEAD of the worktree, both read through gitutil._git_in; a failed rev-parse leaves the keys absent.
2. merge.merge(): after the rebase, when pool config [merge].skip_regate_when_unmoved (default True; read via pool_config().get('merge', {}), import lazily like merge.py's other config reads) and pipeline.gated_target_sha == rev-parse(target) taken before the rebase and rev-parse HEAD of the worktree after the rebase == pipeline.gated_head: skip gate.run_gate, set result['gate'] = 'reused_green' and pipeline.merge_gate = {'mode': 'reused_green', 'gated_target_sha': ..., 'gated_head': ...}; otherwise run the gate as today and record pipeline.merge_gate = {'mode': 'ran'}. Never reuse when the task was held gate_timeout or gate_red after the stamp (the stamp is only written on green, and a later red clears gated_at via clear_stage, so check that gated_at is present). A result marked synthetic_commit must never reuse (always run the gate).
3. orchestrator status / notify: one notify line '<id>: merge reused the daemon gate (target unmoved)' when reused.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_merge.py tests patch gate.run_gate and assert it was called (grep 'run_gate' in tests/test_merge.py): those tasks have no gated_target_sha, so they keep running the gate; tests/test_daemon.py gate tests assert the gated_at stamp (grep 'gated_at'): unchanged plus the two new keys. Run tests/test_merge.py and tests/test_daemon.py.

Depends on B6 T-1551 (daemon.py and merge.py chain). Out of scope: gate.py, spawn.py.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number. Every test named in the acceptance must exist in the diff; the gate checks for them by id.

Re-filed 2026-10-02 11:52 (replaces T-1512): B6 re-filed as T-1551; depends_on re-pointed; spec, acceptance and scope unchanged.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_gate_records_target_sha_and_head_on_green: passes: after a green daemon gate the task's pipeline holds gated_at, gated_target_sha equal to the goal branch head and gated_head equal to the worktree HEAD; a red gate writes neither

tests/test_merge.py::test_merge_reuses_daemon_gate_when_target_unmoved: passes: with gate.run_gate patched, merge.merge on a task whose pipeline.gated_target_sha equals the target head and whose rebase is a no-op does not call run_gate, merges, returns gate 'reused_green' and records pipeline.merge_gate mode 'reused_green'; when the target moved, when gated_head differs from HEAD after the rebase, when gated_at is absent, when the result is marked synthetic_commit, or when [merge].skip_regate_when_unmoved is False, run_gate is called as before

comments.issue: test_merge_reuses_daemon_gate_when_target_unmoved only covers the reuse case. The acceptance also requires run_gate to be called when the target moved, when gated_head differs from HEAD after the rebase, when gated_at is absent, when the result is marked synthetic_commit, and when skip_regate_when_unmoved is False. None of these has a test, so the guard conditions in merge.merge can be removed without any test failing.

The synthetic_commit check reads t.get('synthetic_commit') and pipeline.get('synthetic_commit'). The spec says 'a result marked synthetic_commit', and the diff does not show where that marker lives. If it sits on a different field, reuse would not be blocked. A test would settle this.

pipeline.merge_gate = {'mode': 'ran'} is written only on the final success path. Tasks that hold on gate_red or gate_timeout record no merge_gate mode. The spec says to record 'ran' when the gate runs, so this is a small deviation.
